StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDamageReceived.rationale: SlumberPower.cs:21-32 is AfterDamageReceived and cmds.py:121-122 is the matching sim slot, killing-blow guard included (CreatureCmd.cs:392). C# Decrements and, at Amount <= 0, Stuns with WakeUpMove; the sim decrements, _expire()s and calls owner.wake_up(stunned=True), and monsters/hive/slumbering_beetle.py's wake_up removes the Plating, forces ROLL_OUT_MOVE and stuns. C# relies on PowerCmd.Decrement -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount (PowerModel.cs:478-489) to drop the power at 0 where the sim calls _expire() explicitly -- same observable. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterRemoved.rationale: SlumberPower.cs:34-38 is `SfxCmd.StopLoop(".../slumbering_beetle_sleep_loop")` and nothing else -- presentation only. Recorded rather than skipped because it is the one behavioural-looking AfterRemoved override in this batch, and it is what makes the `_expire()`-for-PowerCmd.Remove substitution used on sibling units a real (if currently unobservable) risk.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called ONCE for the whole enemy side (CombatManager.cs:1256) after every enemy has moved; the sim implements it with the PER-ENEMY slot on_enemy_turn_end (combat.py:341), which fires immediately after each enemy's own move. The sim HAS the side-scoped slot and does not use it here: on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). turn_structure gap G5 (the enemy side is per-enemy in the sim, per-side in the game) is the owning record and carries the identical `gap` verdict; not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3. DORMANT, and the dormancy is EXECUTED rather than asserted -- see `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py rosters` and `enemy-hook-order`. This is the SECOND of the three units the power report's section 6 said would settle turn_structure G5, and the interesting one, because SLUMBERING_BEETLE_NORMAL is a THREE-enemy encounter -- executed: `rosters` gives order=['BowlbugRock', 'BowlbugSilk', 'SlumberingBeetle']. It still settles DORMANT, for a reason G5 does not give: the Slumber owner is the LAST creature in the enemy list, so its per-creature turn-end slot is immediately adjacent to the side-end slot and no other enemy acts in between. `enemy-hook-order` records the sim's actual dispatch as ['clear:BowlbugRock', 'start:BowlbugRock', 'end:BowlbugRock', 'clear:BowlbugSilk', ..., 'end:SlumberingBeetle', 'side_end']. The BLOCK-clear half of G5 is separately dormant here: neither Bowlbug move grants block to an ally (monsters/hive/bowlbugs.py:87 gains block on `self`), so the sim clearing the beetle's block only after the Bowlbugs have moved cannot lose block the game kept. Trigger: reordering the encounter so the beetle is not last, or a Bowlbug-style ally-block move.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2166 `target is self.owner and amount > 0`. See the AfterDamageReceived entry on UnblockedDamage vs the sim's post-modify_hp_lost hp_lost -- equal for this owner, whose only HP-shaped power is Plating (block, not an HP-loss modifier).

guards.what: Decrementing TWICE in one round (damage tick + side-end tick)
guards.rationale: Both sources decrement once per damaging hit AND once at the owner's side end, so a beetle hit twice on the player's turn burns all 3 Slumber and wakes in the same round. Recorded because the sim's docstring (powers.py:2142-2143) phrases it as "each point of unblocked damage", where it is really each damage INSTANCE -- which matches C# but reads as if it did not.

guards.what: stunned=True vs stunned=False as the only difference between the two paths
guards.rationale: C#'s damage wake calls CreatureCmd.Stun(owner, WakeUpMove, "ROLL_OUT_MOVE") (SlumberPower.cs:29) and the natural wake calls WakeUpMove directly with no stun (SlumberPower.cs:48); powers.py:2156 threads exactly that distinction through wake_up(stunned=...). Faithful and non-obvious.
